relevance_note: Table 4 lists three leukocyte adhesion deficiency patients individually (sex, age, CD18/CD11 result), two with ITGB2 variants: "| 12 | F | 2 yr | CD18/CD11 | 0.0 | 99.9 | ITGB2 | c.533C > T".
method_note: Single-centre PID flow-cytometry cohort (60 patients). Only the three LAD patients of Table 4 (rows Patient 12, 13, 14; Patient column holds bare numbers, so labels are 'Table 4 #n') are in scope; all other patients have other PIDs and get no rows. Table 4 prints patient 13 on two rows, one per ITGB2 variant (c.533C > T and c.82_95del14); recorded as one person with two variant rows. Patient 14 has genetic test NT but is in the table of LAD patients with presumptive LAD1 diagnosis by FCM, so included with no variant row. The Inheritance column value 'AR' is the mode of inheritance, not variant origin; inheritance left 'not reported'. Zygosity is not stated (patient 12 shows one variant only; patient 13 two variants without the words compound heterozygous); left 'not reported'. Variant type not stated; not derived from HGVS. Table 4 'Age' column has no footnote defining which age it is (Tables 2 and 3 define age at IVIG start); recorded as age at last evaluation/report, uncertain. Clinical features are given only as a group list: 'The 3 patients who manifested omphalitis, otitis media or mastoiditis' does not say which patient had which feature, so no feature rows and all checklist items 'not reported' (omphalitis, otitis media included). The only per-person phenotype recorded is absent CD18/CD11 expression (0.0%) from each patient's own Table 4 row, supported by the text about the 3 patients. 'LOF genetic mutation of the ITGB2 gene in LAD-1' in the Discussion is a general statement, not used for pathogenicity. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper cites refs 12 and 13 next to XL-CGD and STAT1 patients but does not state that they are the same patients, and no prior report is given for the LAD patients. Output built by a short Python script from my reading; spans checked verbatim by script. No contradictions found.
